newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks slip to below 2,300 in early trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks slip to below 2,300 in early trade.

text.p: French shares slipped slightly at the opening on Friday and gave up the 2,300 level, which it had breached on Thursday, in early exchanges.

Traders said the decline was due to profit-taking prompted by some worries about Wall Street. The New York market nearly reached a fresh record close overnight and some dealers are expecting a further rise today. But some economists are warning the market is overvalued.
Francois Chevallier, chief economist at bank Credit National-BFCE, told the La Tribune newspaper the Dow Jones Industrial index was 20 percent overvalued and a sharp correction lay in store for 1997.
"A sharp correction in 1997 seems inevitable to me because I belief that the Dow Jones is overvalued by some 20 percent and should be around 5,300 points," Chevallier SAID.
The London market, closed on Wednesday and Thursday, hit a new record in early trading. Paris had gained 0.62 percent on Thursday.
"There is very little company news today," said a broker.
"I expect Paris to continue its rise on the back of Wall Street. We think Wall Street will hit a fresh record high which will further support French share," he added.
"But there is hardly anybody around, many are still on holidays," the broker added.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 6.90 points or 0.3 percent at 2,296.85 at 0913 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,293 from 2,304 on Thursday's close.
Volume was 380 million francs, foreign shares included, of which 260 million for CAC-40 shares.
Shares in French tobacco group Seita continued to weaken on Friday, after the launch of a second French lawsuit claiming damages for a cancer death.
Seita stock traded down 1.34 percent to 214.10 francs at 0924 GMT.
